15"""Triton implementation of ``aten::_convert_indices_from_csr_to_coo``. 

16 

17Given compressed row pointers ``crow`` and stored column indices ``col`` 

18sharing the same rank and leading batch extents, the operator decodes the 

19COO coordinate table of the stored entries: shape ``(nd + 2, N * nnz)`` where 

20``nd`` is the batch rank, ``N = prod(lead)``, and ``nnz = col.shape[-1]``. 

21Rows ``0..nd-1`` carry the batch coordinate of leading dim ``k``, the next 

22row carries X and the last row carries Y, with ``(X, Y) = (row, col)`` -- 

23or ``(col, row)`` when ``transpose=True``. The output is int64, or int32 with 

24``out_int32=True``, and C-contiguous. 

25 

26The row of entry ``p`` inside a batch block is 

27``searchsorted_right(crow_block, p) - 1`` (row pointers ascending), evaluated 

28by an exact fixed-trip bisection, one lane per stored entry. Entries beyond 

29the block's last pointer clamp to the last row, matching the native decoder. 

30Batch bases come from the declared strides, so non-contiguous inputs are read 

31correctly with no data movement; the two operands may even use different 

32dtypes. The per-dim leading extents and strides are passed as small int64 

33device tensors, so any batch rank is handled by the same kernel. 

34""" 

35 

36import functools 

37import logging 

38 

39import torch 

40import triton 

41import triton.language as tl 

42 

43logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) 

44 

45# Index dtypes the native operator accepts; floats, bool and complex have no 

46# kernel and are rejected by the wrapper. 

47_ALLOWED_DTYPES = (torch.int8, torch.uint8, torch.int16, torch.int32, torch.int64) 

48 

49# Stored entries per program. The wide tile keeps the CTA count low on large 

50# tables; eight warps spread it as eight int64 lanes per thread. 

51_BLOCK = 2048 

52_NUM_WARPS = 8 

53# grid.x hardware limit (grid.y and grid.z are limited to 255 each); larger 

54# launches are rejected by the backend. 

55_MAX_GRID = 65535 

56 

57 

58@triton.jit 

59def _csr_to_coo_kernel( 

60 crow_ptr, 

61 col_ptr, 

62 out_ptr, 

63 ext_ptr, 

64 crow_stride_ptr, 

65 col_stride_ptr, 

66 bdiv_ptr, 

67 nnz, 

68 n_rows, 

69 total, 

70 nd, 

71 crow_ls, 

72 col_ls, 

73 steps, 

74 BLOCK: tl.constexpr, 

75 OUT_INT32: tl.constexpr, 

76 TRANSPOSE: tl.constexpr, 

77): 

78 # Two-dimensional launch: grid.x alone caps at 65535, i.e. ~134M stored 

79 # entries at BLOCK = 2048, which user tables can exceed. Flattening the 

80 # two program ids keeps one CTA per tile for any table size. A 

81 # grid-stride loop is deliberately not used here: gcu-compiler 

82 # miscompiles a runtime-trip loop carrying several int64 accumulators 

83 # (the batch-base sums and the bisection bounds below) when it is nested 

84 # inside another runtime-trip loop -- from the second outer iteration on 

85 # the decoded rows are wrong. Two-dimensional grids remove the nesting. 

86 tile_id = (tl.program_id(0) + tl.program_id(1) * tl.num_programs(0)).to(tl.int64) 

87 e = tile_id * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK).to(tl.int64) 

88 m = e < total 

89 

90 b = e // nnz 

91 p = (e % nnz).to(tl.int64) 

92 

93 # Per-entry batch base offsets and batch-coordinate planes. ``bdiv[k]`` 

94 # is prod(lead[k+1:]), so the row-major coordinate of dim k is 

95 # (b // bdiv[k]) % lead[k]. The row-base and column-base sums are kept 

96 # in separate loops on purpose: gcu-compiler miscompiles two 

97 # simultaneously live int64 accumulators inside one runtime-trip loop, 

98 # making the first one end up holding the second one's value 

99 # element-for-element (seen with int32 and int64 accumulators alike). 

100 cb = tl.zeros((BLOCK,), dtype=tl.int64) 

101 total64 = tl.full((), total, tl.int64) 

102 for k in range(nd): 

103 coord = (b // tl.load(bdiv_ptr + k)) % tl.load(ext_ptr + k) 

104 cb += coord * tl.load(crow_stride_ptr + k) 

105 tl.store( 

106 out_ptr + k * total64 + e, 

107 coord.to(out_ptr.dtype.element_ty), 

108 mask=m, 

109 ) 

110 vb = tl.zeros((BLOCK,), dtype=tl.int64) 

111 for k in range(nd): 

112 coord = (b // tl.load(bdiv_ptr + k)) % tl.load(ext_ptr + k) 

113 vb += coord * tl.load(col_stride_ptr + k) 

114 

115 # Exact residual bisection: row = searchsorted_right(crow_block, p) - 1. 

116 # The last row pointer is the block's sentinel, so the bracket is 

117 # [0, R). 

118 lo = tl.zeros((BLOCK,), dtype=tl.int32) 

119 hi = tl.zeros((BLOCK,), dtype=tl.int32) + n_rows 

120 for _ in range(steps): 

121 mid = (lo + hi) >> 1 

122 valid = m & (mid < n_rows) 

123 mv = tl.load(crow_ptr + cb + mid.to(tl.int64) * crow_ls, mask=valid, other=0) 

124 c = valid & (mv.to(tl.int32) <= p) 

125 lo = tl.where(c, mid + 1, lo) 

126 hi = tl.where(c, hi, mid) 

127 

128 row = (lo - 1).to(tl.int64) 

129 colv = tl.load(col_ptr + vb + p * col_ls, mask=m, other=0).to(tl.int64) 

130 

131 if TRANSPOSE: 

132 x = colv 

133 y = row 

134 else: 

135 x = row 

136 y = colv 

137 if OUT_INT32: 

138 x = x.to(tl.int32) 

139 y = y.to(tl.int32) 

140 nd64 = tl.full((), nd, tl.int64) 

141 tl.store(out_ptr + nd64 * total64 + e, x.to(out_ptr.dtype.element_ty), mask=m) 

142 tl.store( 

143 out_ptr + (nd64 + 1) * total64 + e, 

144 y.to(out_ptr.dtype.element_ty), 

145 mask=m, 

146 ) 

147 

148 

149@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=128) 

150def _metadata_arrays(nd, extents, crow_strides, col_strides, device): 

151 """Build the small int64 metadata tensors once per (shape, stride) pair. 

152 

153 Allocating four device tensors per call dominates the launch cost of this 

154 memory-light operator, so the arrays are shared across calls with the same 

155 geometry; the values depend only on shape, stride and device. 

156 """ 

157 extents = list(extents) 

158 crow_strides = list(crow_strides) 

159 col_strides = list(col_strides) 

160 # bdiv[k] = prod(extents[k + 1:]) -- 1 for the innermost dim. 

161 divisors = [1] * nd 

162 for k in range(nd - 2, -1, -1): 

163 divisors[k] = divisors[k + 1] * extents[k + 1] 

164 

165 def to_dev(values): 

166 return torch.tensor(values, dtype=torch.int64, device=device) 

167 

168 return ( 

169 to_dev(extents), 

170 to_dev(crow_strides), 

171 to_dev(col_strides), 

172 to_dev(divisors), 

173 ) 

174 

175 

176def _batch_metadata(crow, col, nd): 

177 """Per-dim leading extents / strides and row-major batch divisors.""" 

178 device = crow.device 

179 extents = tuple(int(crow.shape[k]) for k in range(nd)) 

180 crow_strides = tuple(int(crow.stride(k)) for k in range(nd)) 

181 col_strides = tuple(int(col.stride(k)) for k in range(nd)) 

182 return _metadata_arrays(nd, extents, crow_strides, col_strides, device) 

183 

184 

185def _launch(crow, col, out_int32, transpose, out): 

186 # The GCU400 gcu-compiler triggers a `relocation R_DTU_ADDR16_LO_ICALL ... tops_cvt_v2_si64_to_v8_si64` 

187 # link error when vectorizing si64 conversions for int8/uint8/int16 indices. Here the host promotes 

188 # narrow integer indices uniformly to int32 before the Triton kernel: the value range is constrained by 

189 # aten semantics, so promotion does not change values and avoids this compiler defect. 

190 _narrow_index_dtypes = (torch.int8, torch.uint8, torch.int16) 

191 if crow.dtype in _narrow_index_dtypes: 

192 crow = crow.to(torch.int32) 

193 if col.dtype in _narrow_index_dtypes: 

194 col = col.to(torch.int32) 

195 nd = crow.dim() - 1 

196 crow_shape = crow.shape 

197 for k in range(nd): 

198 if crow_shape[k] != col.shape[k]: 

199 raise RuntimeError( 

200 "The size of tensor a (%d) must match the size of tensor b (%d) " 

201 "at non-singleton dimension %d" % (crow_shape[k], col.shape[k], k) 

202 ) 

203 r = int(crow_shape[-1]) - 1 

204 nnz = int(col.shape[-1]) 

205 n_batch = 1 

206 for d in crow_shape[:nd]: 

207 n_batch *= int(d) 

208 total = n_batch * nnz 

209 

210 out_dtype = torch.int32 if out_int32 else torch.int64 

211 if out is None: 

212 out = torch.empty((nd + 2, total), dtype=out_dtype, device=crow.device) 

213 else: 

214 if out.dtype != out_dtype: 

215 raise RuntimeError( 

216 f"Expected out tensor to have dtype {out_dtype}, but got {out.dtype}" 

217 ) 

218 if tuple(out.shape) != (nd + 2, total): 

219 out.resize_((nd + 2, total)) 

220 

221 if total == 0: 

222 return out 

223 

224 ext, crow_strides, col_strides, divisors = _batch_metadata(crow, col, nd) 

225 # Cap each grid dimension at the hardware limit (grid.x 65535, grid.y 255) 

226 # and let grid.y carry the overflow so one CTA still owns exactly one 

227 # tile. 65535 * 255 tiles cover ~3.4e10 entries, far beyond any 

228 # allocatable output table. 

229 num_tiles = triton.cdiv(total, _BLOCK) 

230 grid_x = min(num_tiles, _MAX_GRID) 

231 grid_y = triton.cdiv(num_tiles, grid_x) 

232 grid = (grid_x, grid_y) 

233 _csr_to_coo_kernel[grid]( 

234 crow, 

235 col, 

236 out, 

237 ext, 

238 crow_strides, 

239 col_strides, 

240 divisors, 

241 nnz, 

242 r, 

243 total, 

244 nd, 

245 crow.stride(-1), 

246 col.stride(-1), 

247 max(r.bit_length(), 1), 

248 BLOCK=_BLOCK, 

249 OUT_INT32=bool(out_int32), 

250 TRANSPOSE=bool(transpose), 

251 num_warps=_NUM_WARPS, 

252 ) 

253 return out 

254 

255 

256def _convert_indices_from_csr_to_coo( 

257 crow_indices, col_indices, *, out_int32=False, transpose=False, out=None 

258): 

259 """Decode COO coordinates from CSR row pointers and column indices. 

260 

261 ``aten::_convert_indices_from_csr_to_coo(Tensor crow_indices, 

262 Tensor col_indices, *, bool out_int32=False, bool transpose=False) 

263 -> Tensor``. The result has shape ``(nd + 2, N * nnz)`` and is int64 

264 unless ``out_int32=True``. 

265 """ 

266 logger.debug("GEMS_ENFLAME_GCU400 _CONVERT_INDICES_FROM_CSR_TO_COO") 

267 if not isinstance(out_int32, bool): 

268 raise TypeError(f"out_int32 must be a bool, got {type(out_int32).__name__}") 

269 if not isinstance(transpose, bool): 

270 raise TypeError(f"transpose must be a bool, got {type(transpose).__name__}") 

271 crow = crow_indices 

272 col = col_indices 

273 for name, t in (("crow_indices", crow), ("col_indices", col)): 

274 if not isinstance(t, torch.Tensor): 

275 raise TypeError( 

276 f"_convert_indices_from_csr_to_coo: {name} must be a Tensor, " 

277 f"got {type(t).__name__}" 

278 ) 

279 if t.dtype not in _ALLOWED_DTYPES: 

280 raise NotImplementedError( 

281 '"convert_indices_from_csr_to_coo_cuda" not implemented for ' 

282 f"'{str(t.dtype).replace('torch.', '')}'" 

283 ) 

284 if crow.dim() == 0 or col.dim() == 0: 

285 raise IndexError("Dimension specified as -1 but tensor has no dimensions") 

286 if crow.dim() != col.dim(): 

287 raise RuntimeError( 

288 "crow_indices and col_indices are supposed to have the same " 

289 "dimensionality, but got %d and %d dimensional tensors, " 

290 "respectively." % (crow.dim(), col.dim()) 

291 ) 

292 # gcu400 cannot link the 8-bit -> int64 conversion helper used by the 

293 # masked gather (ld.lld: relocation R_DTU_ADDR16_LO_ICALL against 

294 # tops_cvt_v2_si64_to_v8_si64__4). Widening the two index tensors on the 

295 # host keeps every value exact and avoids that codegen path entirely. 

296 if crow.dtype in (torch.int8, torch.uint8) or col.dtype in ( 

297 torch.int8, 

298 torch.uint8, 

299 ): 

300 crow = crow.to(torch.int32) 

301 col = col.to(torch.int32) 

302 return _launch(crow, col, out_int32, transpose, out) 

303 

304 

305def _convert_indices_from_csr_to_coo_out( 

306 crow_indices, col_indices, *, out_int32=False, transpose=False, out 

307): 

308 """``aten::_convert_indices_from_csr_to_coo.out``: write into ``out``.""" 

309 logger.debug("GEMS_ENFLAME_GCU400 _CONVERT_INDICES_FROM_CSR_TO_COO_OUT") 

310 if not isinstance(out, torch.Tensor): 

311 raise TypeError( 

312 "_convert_indices_from_csr_to_coo.out: out must be a Tensor, got " 

313 f"{type(out).__name__}" 

314 ) 

315 return _convert_indices_from_csr_to_coo( 

316 crow_indices, 

317 col_indices, 

318 out_int32=out_int32, 

319 transpose=transpose, 

320 out=out, 

321 )
